title: Mars Matrix
body: The logo and the loading, OK and NG screens from the Japanese disc, and two the game never shows, Saving and Searching: it says it's loading whatever it does with the card.

title: Grandia 2
body: The logo and the three memory card messages, NG, OK and accessing, every screen the game puts on the VMU, from the Japanese and European discs, which differ in the logo and the accessing message. They sit in the program turned upside down, as the VMU takes them.

title: Spider-Man
body: Spider-Man's mask, which the VMU rests on, and the saving, loading, OK and failed screens, from the American disc, where each is a small Windows bitmap of its own.

title: Resident Evil 2
body: Every VMU screen from the European and Japanese discs, in English, French and Japanese, including the status screen with its blinking condition, and the weapon names and digits it's built from; the art is hidden in the Windows CE program's resources. The discs also have four more save icons and confirm the nine already here.

title: Guilty Gear X
body: The logo, the one screen the game ever puts on the VMU, from the Japanese disc, and two more save icons: the save's icon changes with what's been unlocked. The disc also shows the icon already here is the one for Dizzy.

title: Resident Evil 3: Nemesis
body: Every VMU screen from the Japanese and European discs, which differ only in the title: the portraits, the memory card messages, the condition monitor's heartbeat in each of its nine states and one screen the game never shows. The discs also show which save icon is Japan's and which the West's.

title: Cool Cool Toon
body: The Story, logo, Save, Notty and Flitz screens from the Japanese disc, and three more save icons, the boy's, girl's and woman's portraits, unpacked from the files the disc keeps them in. The disc also shows the save icon already here is the man's.

title: Napple Tale: Arsia in Daydream
body: The logo and the saving, loading, OK, failed and in-use messages the game shows on the VMU, the small font of its score display, and its two save icons, from the Japanese disc.

title: Space Channel 5 and Space Channel 5: Part 2
body: Each game's Channel 5 logo, which the VMU rests on, and its loading and saving screens from the Japanese discs, and in the first game a Sibuya sign from the staff roll and eleven character portraits, ten of them not yet identified. The discs also confirm both save icons already here are the games' own.

title: Rainbow Cotton
body: Eleven animations from the Japanese disc: the title logo, Now loading, and Cotton blinking, seeing stars, dizzy and talking. The disc also confirms the save icon already here is the game's own.

title: Border Down
body: The SDF logo and the hit counter the game keeps on the VMU during play, with its digits, and the save icon, from the Japanese disc.

title: Tokyo Bus Guide
body: The bus, Danger and Now loading screens from the Japanese disc, and the traffic sign quiz the game writes to the VMU: its title with the scrolling credits, its 63 road signs and its font, a version screen it never shows, and its save icon.

title: Super Puzzle Fighter II X for Matching Service
body: The logo and ACCESS screens and the save icon from the Japanese disc, with OK and ERROR screens the game carries but never shows.

title: Vampire Chronicle for Matching Service
body: The logo and ACCESS screens and the save icon from the Japanese disc, with OK and ERROR screens the game carries but never shows.

title: Virtua Tennis 2
body: Eleven screens from the European disc, which carries the logos of all three releases: Virtua Tennis 2, Japan's Power Smash 2 and the US Tennis 2K2. The game turns its logo into place in 3D, redrawn here from its own renderer.

title: Capcom vs. SNK: Millennium Fight 2000
body: The logo and ACCESS screens and five save icons from the Japanese disc, among them the replays' and the colour edit file's. The disc also shows the memory card icon was made with a tool, not by the game.

title: Tech Romancer
body: The logo and ACCESS screens from the Japanese disc, and the menus, rules and score screens of Kikaioh Mini, the VMU game it carries. The disc also confirms both save icons already in the archive.

title: The Japanese VMU
body: The main menu, big font and clock animals of the first VMUs, sold in Japan in 1998, read from their own BIOS. Its clock has a cat's paw prints and a helicopter where the later VMU has a dog and a bird.

title: Sonic Shuffle
body: The logo screen redrawn from the Japanese disc, an unused NO CARD screen, and the sheet of cards and digits the game builds your hand from.

title: Metropolis Street Racer
body: Three screens from the European disc, and a small text font the game carries but never uses.

title: Resident Evil Code: Veronica
body: Nineteen screens from the Japanese and European discs, including the portraits and the condition monitor with its heartbeat. The disc also shows which save icon is Claire's and which is Chris's.

title: Search by any of a game's names
body: Games are now found by their other names too, like Jet Grind Radio for Jet Set Radio, and show their English title with the Japanese one beneath. The Japanese flag now marks only what's in the Japanese release alone.

title: Marvel vs. Capcom 2, and VS.COM
body: Screens from the Japanese disc, including VS.COM, the VMU program the game copies to the memory card, with its sprites and three more save icons.

title: Game pages in tabs
body: A game's screens, sprites, fonts and notes are now tabs on its page; press 1 to 4 to switch.

title: Save icons
body: A new page for the colour icons the Dreamcast's file menu shows for each save: 520 icons from 344 games, searchable in one grid.

title: Jet Set Radio, and its graffiti viewer
body: Twelve screens from the Japanese disc, including the graffiti viewer the game copies to the VMU, with its fonts and sprites.

title: Sprites, out from behind the scenes
body: The smaller art games draw onto part of a screen, like digits, fonts and faces, now has its own card on each game's page.

title: Falcon's course, scrolling down
body: Screens can now scroll down as well as sideways, starting with a whole lap of Power Stone Mini's Falcon game.

title: Power Stone Mini
body: The VMU game hidden in Power Stone's program: its title, portraits and the screens of its three minigames.

title: Shenmue's Goodies
body: 213 animated Shenmue characters, the Goodies Shenmue Passport traded online until 2002, from the Neoseeker Shenmue wiki, and the VMU program from the Passport disc that showed them. Their timing hasn't been checked against the game.

title: Shenmue and Shenmue II, straight from the disc
body: Shenmue's title logo and 70 Man Battle screens, and every VMU screen in Shenmue II, from the Japanese discs.

title: The VMU's own main menu
body: The screen the VMU shows with no game, read from the US BIOS along with its clock animals and fonts.

title: Shinseiki Evangelion: Typing E-Keikaku
body: Every VMU screen in Gainax's Evangelion typing game, the first Windows CE game in the archive.

title: Crazy Taxi 2
body: Every VMU screen in the US release, including the title's dancing flames.

title: The rest of Ikaruga
body: Every other VMU screen from the Japanese disc, including the chain counter and an unused Load screen.

title: Street Fighter III: 3rd Strike, straight from the disc
body: Every VMU screen in the Japanese release.

title: Browse by game
body: The archive now opens on a searchable grid of games, each with its own page. Old links still work.

title: Sakura Taisen 3, with scrolling banners
body: Everything on the Japanese disc: the title, crest, minigame intros and blinking character expressions, and the 23 special attack banners the game scrolls across the VMU in battle.

title: Soul Calibur's fighters
body: All 19 fighters, five poses each, decompressed from the US disc.

title: Power Stone and Power Stone 2, straight from the disc
body: Every VMU screen in both games.

title: Project Justice, straight from the disc
body: Every VMU screen in the Japanese Moero! Justice Gakuen.

title: Bangai-O, straight from the disc
body: Every VMU screen in the Japanese Bangaioh, from the title screen and its animated robot to four screens the game never shows, played with the game's own timing.

title: Berserk, straight from the disc
body: Every Puck screen, played with the game's own timing, including seven new animations and six unused screens.

title: Ryo Hazuki comes to life
body: Shenmue's Ryo Hazuki is now animated, and you can filter the screens by game.

title: Carrier
body: The title screen from Jaleco's survival horror.

title: Sega Tetris
body: The title screen, memory card screens and the full animated cast.

title: Title screens and the first animations
body: Title screens from six more games and the first animated screens, which play on hover and download as GIF or animated SVG.

title: Tony Hawk's Pro Skater
body: All 35 screens, from "Rad" to "U suck".

title: The archive opens
body: The first 128 screens, from the Puyo Pop Fever cast to Sonic Adventure.
